Guidance Note: Written notices given under or in connection with the agreement. As such, it is important that prior to signing the agreement the parties agree how those notices are to be given and provide each other with the correct contact details. Landlords are required by law (section 48 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1987) to give an address for these purposes (which can be their agent’s address if the property is being managed by an agent). Additionally, this section has been drafted so as to allow landlords and tenants to agree that certain notices given under or in connection with the agreement may be sent via email, except a notice given by the landlord under section 8 (notice of proceedings for possession) or section 21 (recovery of possession on expiry or termination of assured shorthold tenancy) of the Housing Act 1988 which should always be given to the tenant in hard copy at the property.

Claimant’s date of birth and National Insurance number (for the Compensation Recovery Unit): 14 July 2003, EW 78 17 48 B

We are instructed by the above named to claim damages in connection with a road traffic accident on 02 June 2020 at Victoria Park.

Please confirm the identity of your insurers. Please note that the insurers will need to see this letter as soon as possible and it may affect your insurance cover and/or the conduct of any subsequent legal proceedings if you do not send this letter to them.

Clear summary of the facts

The circumstances of the accident are:

Our client was driving a works van and had stopped at a red light when the vehicle you were driving collided with the rear of Ó Súilleabháin's vehicle.

Liability

The reason why we are alleging fault is:

You failed to keep a proper lookout and drove too close to the vehicle in front.

We are obtaining a police report and will let you have a copy of the same upon your undertaking to meet half the fee.

Injuries

A description of our clients’ injuries is as follows:

Whiplash injury to the neck and upper back, with headaches. Our client cannot lift or carry, cannot care for a young child unaided and has stopped all sport.

Our client (hospital reference number RX44-83500) received treatment for the injuries at the Royal Albion Infirmary.

Our client is still suffering from the effects of Ó Súilleabháin's injuries. We invite you to participate with us in addressing our client’s immediate needs by use of rehabilitation.

Loss of Earnings

Dr Ó Súilleabháin is employed as a delivery driver and has had the following time off work: 24 September 2025 to 22 August 2024. Our client’s approximate weekly income is £3,029.

If you are our client’s employers, please provide us with the usual earnings details which will enable us to calculate our client’s financial loss.

Other Financial Losses

We are also aware of the following likely financial losses:

Damaged clothing and personal effects: £246

Prescription charges: £2,190.56

Travel to hospital and physiotherapy appointments: £3,071.41

Statutory sick pay only has been paid, into our client’s account ending 0918.

Details of the insurer

We have also sent a letter of claim to Wise Facilities Management Limited, 128 Queen's Place, Little Station, Cardiff, South Glamorgan LS4Y 1TW, and a copy of that letter is attached. We understand their insurers are Severn & Wye Underwriting Ltd, 164 Victoria Lane, NORWICH CR55 1DF (claims number BD540732).

At this stage of our enquiries we would expect the documents contained in parts 1 and 3 of the standard disclosure list to be relevant to this action.

A copy of this letter is attached for you to send to your insurers. Finally we expect an acknowledgment of this letter within 21 days by yourselves or your insurers.

Yours faithfully

L Thomas
Lewis & Grant LLP

Introductory guidance note and checklists

If you intend to rent a home to or from someone, then you should have a written tenancy agreement. To help tenants and landlords, the Government has produced this model tenancy agreement which can be used free of charge. No fee may be charged by anyone for its use.

If you are considering using this agreement, it is very important that you first read this introductory guidance note.

1.1 Why has Government produced this model agreement?

This model tenancy agreement has been developed by the Government with the aim of producing an agreement which strikes a fair balance between the interests of landlords and tenants. There is no legal requirement to use this particular agreement.

This agreement has been designed for those wanting the stability of a longer tenancy. But the Government recognises that the circumstances of either the tenant or the landlord may change during the tenancy which is why, if the agreement is for two years or more, either the landlord or the tenant can bring it to an end earlier where certain conditions apply (see the break clauses in section F).

1.2 Can this agreement be used if we want to enter into an agreement for a fixed term of less than 2 years?
